method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

supports: 088 blurred/changed colour vision during ethambutol warrants stopping exposure, contacting TB team and ophthalmic assessment
sourceChecks.scope: Specific optic-toxicity support, not whole-batch clinical validation.

items.assessment: Sampling-before-antibiotic key is defensible, but drainage-bag option introduces an unstated catheter and may be eliminated without clinical reasoning.
issues: Sampling-before-antibiotic key is defensible, but drainage-bag option introduces an unstated catheter and may be eliminated without clinical reasoning.
proposedChanges: Specify an indwelling catheter and a readily accessible sampling port, or replace bag option with an applicable midstream collection error. Preserve stable/no-delay context.

items.assessment: Stop because organism identified is implausible and always-required broad coverage is a cueing absolute.
issues: Stop because organism identified is implausible and always-required broad coverage is a cueing absolute.
proposedChanges: Use competing plans: complete broad course solely because response is good; repeat culture before any regimen review; add targeted drug while completing broad course. Keep targeted effective-regimen review with susceptibility-specific rationale.

items.assessment: Every antibiotic contraindicated is an implausibly broad allergy inference.
issues: Every antibiotic contraindicated is an implausibly broad allergy inference.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Avoid all penicillins and cephalosporins without asking about the reaction. Explain that reaction details/product-specific assessment are needed rather than equating all related agents automatically.

items.assessment: Diarrhea means antibiotic working and meal-skipping without reassessment are cartoon responses; key is the only reasonable option.
issues: Diarrhea means antibiotic working and meal-skipping without reassessment are cartoon responses; key is the only reasonable option.
proposedChanges: Add stool frequency and hydration context. Use plausible incomplete responses: routine drug-intolerance advice based on absence of fever; delayed stool collection without current hydration/precaution assessment. Keep timely assessment/reporting and explain possible infectious colitis versus mild intolerance.

items.assessment: Clinical/functional improvement at stable oxygen requirement contrasts well with antipyretic masking, somnolence and worsening hypotension; multiple cues drive selection.
New auditory/vestibular symptoms before next gentamicin dose merit report and dose clarification; no need to wait for confirmed loss.
Current renal decline invalidates reliance on predating level; review current exposure/dosing rather than assuming stable clearance.
Pause/assess key is defensible, but faster infusion to shorten reaction is implausibly unsafe.
issues: Pause/assess key is defensible, but faster infusion to shorten reaction is implausibly unsafe.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Slow briefly, then restore the original rate without reporting the reaction. Explain that assessment and an authorized revised plan are required before continued exposure.

items.assessment: Serious painful mucosal rash warrants urgent action, but waiting for peeling or next-week reduced dose are extreme.
issues: Serious painful mucosal rash warrants urgent action, but waiting for peeling or next-week reduced dose are extreme.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Treat mouth sores as thrush separate from a mild skin eruption. Replace option3 with: Request a routine dose reduction while continuing the medicine. Explain that combined mucosal and painful skin findings require urgent severe-reaction assessment.

items.assessment: Food timing/nausea distractor does not address tendon complaint.
issues: Food timing/nausea distractor does not address tendon complaint.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Reduce running distance and discuss the pain at routine follow-up. Explain that new fluoroquinolone-associated tendon pain needs prompt medication review and avoidance of tendon stress.

items.assessment: Crushing all products together to improve absorption is implausible without a swallowing issue.
issues: Crushing all products together to improve absorption is implausible without a swallowing issue.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Separate the antacid but continue calcium with doxycycline. Explain that both mineral sources require product-specific interaction review.

items.assessment: Orange urine without systemic danger cues supports expected rifampin effect with red-flag teaching; competing interpretations are relevant.
Colour/acuity change on ethambutol needs contact before further dosing; BCCDC explicitly supports stopping and prompt assessment of optic toxicity.
All distractors are implausible: double isoniazid, stop all TB drugs permanently, tingling means cure.
issues: All distractors are implausible: double isoniazid, stop all TB drugs permanently, tingling means cure.
proposedChanges: Replace with: restart pyridoxine and wait until routine visit to report; request symptom relief without reporting missed pyridoxine; attribute tingling to footwear and continue regimen without review. Keep assessment/report key, similar option lengths, and explain possible neuropathy.

items.assessment: Exploring tolerability/support and preserving prescribed combination addresses a real adherence choice; self-selected single tablet and delayed catch-up fail regimen integrity.
Only reasonable correct route explanation is cued by exaggerated IV-always-better and oral-no-adverse-effects claims.
issues: Only reasonable correct route explanation is cued by exaggerated IV-always-better and oral-no-adverse-effects claims.
proposedChanges: Use balanced misconceptions: IV would be preferred if access were easier; routes can be exchanged at the same dose; oral therapy is reserved only for mild disease. Shorten key to Oral treatment reaches the intestinal infection site and explain site-specific distribution.

items.assessment: Observed immediate swallowing undermines oral surface contact; product-directed local administration is defensible with realistic dilution/rinsing errors.
Fluconazole/warfarin interaction needs monitoring plan; food compensation and dose spacing do not resolve metabolism-based effect.
Skin-rash-only monitoring is unrelated filler for explicit QT/hypokalemia risk.
issues: Skin-rash-only monitoring is unrelated filler for explicit QT/hypokalemia risk.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Check pulse regularity alone and proceed if it is regular. Explain that a current regular pulse does not evaluate QT interval or remove electrolyte-related risk.

items.assessment: The pharmacist already identifies unspecified statin interaction, so item only repeats generic clarify-alert objective without drug-specific reasoning.
issues: The pharmacist already identifies unspecified statin interaction, so item only repeats generic clarify-alert objective without drug-specific reasoning.
proposedChanges: Name simvastatin and ask which toxicity assessment/teaching is particularly relevant after a new clarithromycin prescription, using balanced competing adverse-effect clusters. Key should target muscle injury and appropriate regimen review; source-check product contraindication/management.

items.assessment: Ramipril plus trimethoprim and elevated potassium require reporting combined potassium-retaining effect; dose spacing does not remove pharmacodynamic risk.
Arbitrary full-day feed interruption is overtly signalled as wrong.
issues: Arbitrary full-day feed interruption is overtly signalled as wrong.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Apply the same two-hour feed hold used for another antibiotic without checking this product. Explain that timing depends on drug formulation/interaction and nutrition needs.

items.assessment: Extra nitrofurantoin for kidney penetration is an implausible remedy; key is the only reasonable clinical response.
issues: Extra nitrofurantoin for kidney penetration is an implausible remedy; key is the only reasonable clinical response.
proposedChanges: Use credible competing plans: request a urinary analgesic for flank discomfort; continue a lower-UTI plan after antiemetic relief; arrange routine repeat urine testing instead of prompt systemic assessment. Specify fever/flank signs and explain poor suitability of a bladder-focused regimen for possible upper infection.

items.assessment: Prescribed duration subject to clinician change and severe-effect reporting are appropriate; sharing/storing leftovers are realistic patient teaching misconceptions.
Observed aseptic technique and complication reporting demonstrate home readiness; bag colour and alarm reliance are credible incomplete safety strategies.

rubricUpdate: Includes user-requested assessment of longest/most-comprehensive key cues, only-reasonable-option bias, parallel option grammar and case-specific reasoning.
hashRevalidationReason: Author metadata/self-audit update overlapped the first-pass review window. Do not use recorded hashes as current approval until snapshot revalidation.
